verdicts.claim: A checkpoint copies committed WAL content back into the main database
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: "A checkpoint operation takes content from the WAL file and transfers it back into the original database file."

verdicts.claim: SQLite documents automatic checkpointing at 1000 WAL pages by default, triggered by a commit that reaches the threshold
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: "automatically checkpoint whenever a COMMIT occurs that causes the WAL file to be 1000 pages or more in size"; pragma.html: "enabled by default with an interval of 1000"

verdicts.claim: the threshold can be changed or auto-checkpointing disabled
verdicts.evidence: pragma.html: "Setting the auto-checkpoint size to zero or a negative value turns auto-checkpointing off."

verdicts.claim: The current pragma documentation was updated 2026-10-04
Automatic checkpoints use PASSIVE mode; passive does as much work as possible without waiting and can leave frames uncheckpointed
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: "All checkpoints initiated by sqlite3_wal_checkpoint() and by the automatic checkpoint mechanism are PASSIVE"; c3ref: "passive mode might leave the checkpoint unfinished if there are concurrent readers or writers"

verdicts.claim: APSW Connection.wal_checkpoint(dbname, mode) defaults the mode to PASSIVE and returns WAL frame and checkpointed-frame counts
verdicts.evidence: APSW: "wal_checkpoint(dbname=None, mode=apsw.SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE) -> tuple[int,int]"; returns "size of the WAL log in frames and the number of frames checkpointed"

verdicts.claim: FULL waits for writers and readers to reach the latest snapshot and blocks new writers
verdicts.evidence: c3ref: "blocks ... until there is no database writer and all readers are reading from the most recent database snapshot ... blocks new database writers while it is pending"

verdicts.claim: RESTART also waits until readers no longer use the WAL; TRUNCATE adds zero-length truncation on success
verdicts.evidence: pragma.html: RESTART "blocks ... until all readers are finished with the log file"; TRUNCATE "the WAL file is truncated to zero bytes upon successful completion"

verdicts.claim: A successful checkpoint usually recycles the WAL for reuse rather than truncating it
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: "The checkpoint does not normally truncate the WAL file ... it merely causes SQLite to start overwriting the WAL file from the beginning."

verdicts.claim: A reader holding an older WAL snapshot can prevent a checkpoint from advancing beyond that reader's end mark; persistent overlapping readers allow unbounded WAL growth
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: "checkpoint must stop when it reaches a page in the WAL that is past the end mark of any current reader" ... "the WAL file will grow without bound"
